item.title: A Sadist Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.description: Just an SCP idea I thought about a long time ago, but I kinda forgot about it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes?

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: My SCP is a dunce cap that can telepathically talk to their victims and tricks them that it's a higher being, and if they do what it demands, they'll be gifted eternal salvation. When the victim completes their task(s), the SCP disappears and leaves them, so they can suffer for what they have done. (So basically, it's a troll)

Central Narrative: In 1990, a man was found dead in his house from suicide. One of his friends went to check on him and saw that the door was unlocked. He decided to enter the house and noticed there were multiple drawings all over the walls and hand-made wooden objects related to the SCP scattered around the room. There was also a message on one of the walls that say this,

"I Don't Understand. I Did Everything It Wanted Me To Do, But I Don't Hear It Anymore. I Made It My God. I Pushed Everyone Away From My Life. I Killed My Own Two Kids For It, And Yet It's Abandons Me. I Guess My Fate Wasn't Good Enough…"

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The cap can somehow teleport to different places in the world, causing more harm to others. The cap does these things to people because it finds it entertaining. The SCP only goes after religious people.

Additional Notes: This might be a boring and cringy SCP idea, so go easy on me lol. (But seriously though, any critique is helpful.)

I don't think I represented my central narrative the right way, but the story is going to be around addendums, interviews, and incidents.

Should I change the object the SCP is? I don't think a dunce cap would fit too well. it seems silly IMO…

item.title: Fireproof Rescue Dog
item.description: A, quite literally, hot dog.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Containment Procedures, Description, Recovered Incident Reports, Email Transcript

Genre: Dramatic, with some lighthearted moments between the dog and it’s handler

Elevator Pitch:

+ Show Elevator Pitch
- Hide Elevator Pitch

This SCP is a former SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. When irritated, the dog is also able to raise its internal body temperature to an unnaturally high level, allowing it to essentially burn those who come into contact with it and spit small sparks. Visually, the dog is a completely average looking dalmatian. Given that it was an SAR animal, the dog had a handler. However, the handler was entirely non-anomalous and ignorant of the animal's abilities. The dog and the handler were close with the local fire department and went on missions almost exclusively related to local fires and their aftermaths.

Central Narrative:

+ Show Central Narrative
- Hide Central Narrative

The central narrative of this SCP Article would be the history of the SCP’s life prior to containment. This would be told through the local fire department’s incident reports recovered by the Foundation, detailing calls the dog was used on and how the dog and it’s handler performed. The reports would be written by the dog’s handler and would detail their specific experiences working with the dog during the incident. The handler is entirely human and simply good at their job. The dog’s anomalous protection does not extend to them nor anything other than itself.

The dog is contained by the Foundation after it gives several children second and third degree burns. This happens because of an off-duty incident when the dog and it’s handler are approached by a mother and her three children while relaxing at a park. The handler is distracted talking with the mother, while the children entertain themselves with the dog. Eventually, the dog becomes irritated by the attention and attacks them, biting one child and barking at the rest. This would result in the bitten child having a severe third degree burn from the bite and the other two children having small second degree burns from the dog’s saliva, sprayed from its barking. This portion of the story would be told by a hospital’s incident report that is also recovered by the Foundation.

This incident is what alerts the Foundation to the dog’s existence. The dog is subsequently contained, with it’s handler and any witnesses to the incident are anesthetized.

The article would end several years after the dog is contained, with a researcher in charge of the animal noting its declining health and mental state. The researcher makes a request to their superiors to suggest the dog be used for SAR work once again, this time for the Foundation. This portion of the article is told through an email.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ Show Hook/Attention-Grabber
- Hide Hook/Attention-Grabber

I want the reader to feel bad for this SCP. It’s just an animal born with powers it can’t quite control. The dog only wants to help people and be with its handler, but that can’t be because of the dangers present with its abilities.

Additional Notes:

+ Show Additional Notes
- Hide Additional Notes

My plan is to make this article fairly straightforward and short given that this is my first. I’m not expecting it to be greenlit quite yet, but I would appreciate any continued criticism or suggestion. In particular, whether the concept seems viable or whether I should rewrite the concept entirely.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights) scpwiki.com
item.description: An website forum about a fictional SCP Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Elevator Pitch: scpwiki.com is a website created by The Foundation where creative writers post articles and tales detailing a fictional universe populated by anomalous items, entities and groups of interest, with the SCP Foundation at the heart.

Central Narrative: The Foundation created the website after online discussions of the SCP Foundation emerged, with the aim of protecting the masquerade by decieving people into believing it was fictional. However, a shift from SCP-507 reveals it to be anomalous, and responsible for creating events and anomalies in an alternate universe and its own SCP Foundation, leaving The Foundation to ponder if they are any different.

Hook/ Attention-Grabber: I want to ask a question that (please correct me if I'm wrong!) I haven't yet seen on the site; what if the Foundation exists in our world, and the site is merely for readers to be decieved into believing it does not exist? It fundamentally links our world and the fictional world in a very literal way.

Additional Notes: Again, I cannot say I am hugely well-read on the site, and so it is possible an article similar to this exists, for which I apologise- it is a coincidence. But I do believe that it has potential (and even considered storing it for when I had more experience writing and proposing it for 001, but I don't think it would stand its ground, and I'm impatient!).

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights) Decieve Me Not
item.description: My first SCP, seeking greenlighting. A humanoid entity, revolving around truth, falsehood, and deception.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

+ Elevator Pitch
- Elevator Pitch

Decieve Me Not is a sapient humanoid entity that is believed to be a unique and poorly understood type of reality bender. It appears to be wearing a crimson robe and a white, porcelain Greek comedy mask. It has near-perfect control over its abilities, but these abilities appear to be limited to a specific few. It can teleport, which is countered by SRAs. Its main anomalous trait, however, is its ability to control and affect minds, which cannot be countered with SRAs. During conversation with the entity, an individual is compelled to tell the truth to any question the entity may ask. The other ability is long term- after viewing or hearing it at a present state (i.e., not through recording or photograph), an individual will undergo anomalous mental changes over three weeks. They will begin to lie intermittently, before eventually losing the ability to tell the truth. They will then seek out conversation with the entity, leading to them lying to it, resulting in [DATA EXPUNGED].

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

The narrative largely revolves around unraveling the nature of the entity, with a short side note of an unfortunate doctor whose life was effectively ruined by its anomalous effects. It strangely appeared in a Foundation site, seemingly willing to be contained and thus interrogated. It takes a number of individuals to be affected until the Foundation can effectively contain it, however, at which point they attempt to unravel its goals and nature, with a certain Foundation doctor being brought in for his ability to combat its anomalous effects and research it. Hints are gradually made throughout the article that it is in fact at the whim of an unidentified, much more powerful reality bender, and that the entity itself aims to make itself more powerful so that he may usurp the more powerful one. Furthermore, more hints (especially the entity's appearance and an O5 classified interview at the end) imply that the entity is linked to The Hanged King, and specifically one of his three lords.

+ Hook/ Attention-Grabber
- Hook/ Attention-Grabber

The article aims to explore the theme of truth and lies, both showing how that may affect normal individuals on a more mundane basis, and how they may be percieved by entities of a higher existence. Furthermore, I hope to hook readers with a gradually unravelling plot of deception, which, even by the end, is not fully explained, leaving readers to their own imagination.

+ Additional Notes
- Additional Notes

The article may seem fairly ambitious for a first time writer, which I understand. I have a few other ideas for SCPs which I will pursue while I await greenlights, and if you believe that the idea is good but do not have faith in a first time writer to properly execute it, I would appreciate that feedback, though I would love the opportunity to put forward a draft.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.description: A humanoid whose anomaly is literally that he cannot be contained.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify)

Page Layout: Alternating between versions of the Uncontainable Man's SCP file and prose sections detailing the Foundation's encounters with him.

Elevator Pitch: A man who literally cannot be contained. If anyone tries to hold him against his will, something will always happen that lets him get out, no matter how many ridiculous coincidences have to happen together. This man is incredibly arrogant and attempts to use this power to toy with the Foundation to get what he wants – at least until he learns why the numebr-one rule of messing with the Foundation is, "Don't."

Central Narrative: The narrative starts with an MTF being dispatched to Somerandomtown County (working name) to investigate reports of a prisoner in the county jail who's anomalously good at escaping. They track down the prisoner, tell him who they are, handcuff him, and take him to Site-8 for containment. After a week, a containment breach occurs at Site-8, letting him out. The MTF recaptures him, and the cycle of containment, escape, and recapture repeats as the Foundation creates harsher and harsher conprocs, until they figure out what's going on and decide to put out a reward for whoever can devise conprocs for this man. Eventually, the captain of the MTF, who at this point is sick of chasing this guy, asks him what the Foundation has to do to contain him. At this point, the guy starts making ridiculous demands to the tune of "you have to contain me in a five-star hotel and give me anything I ask for, no matter how ridiculous-" and then the captain just shoots him. Finally, the article ends with the SCP's updated containment file, with the class as Neutralized and the Special Containment Procedures being, "If it doesn't comply, threaten lethal force."

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Explores what would actually happen if the Foundation encountered an anomaly whose property is that he cannot be contained, and also tries to derive humor from some old Gary Stu cliches ("my original chaructr is a humanid wat will DSTROIE EVERYSANG and BRETCH CONTEINMENT IF THE FONDANTION DOESNT GIV IT WHAT IT WANTS).

Additional Notes:

item.title: (SEEKING GREENLIGHTS) Hold on, why?
item.description: Inforhazard of question
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Typical SCP article including logs of every asked question, their host's reactions, and outcomes.

+Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention Grabber, and Notes
- why?

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly is an infohazard that induces a great sense of curiosity to individuals who have gained any information regarding it. Individuals with knowledge of the SCP initially ask themselves a certain question, regardless of which it is unknown to the individual or not, or classified or not. The subjects have no control over whatever question they ask. That is known as Stage 1 of the "infection". Stage 2 makes the individual have a great urge in research, usually that of the question they asked themselves. In certain individuals, Stage 3 may manifest. Stage 3 is death by insanity, believed to have been caused by the exponential growth of their will to find information or their "ultimate answer" to their questions. Stage 3 is only known to manifest if ever an individual asks themselves a certain impossibility, or possibly classified information. The infohazard is only lethal whenever an individual expires after 3 years of infection.

Central Narrative: The infohazard was detected after a lack of personnel morale. Plenty of personnel was observed asking "why" to themselves, with the situation growing large enough to be taken into consideration by the O5 council. Journals were distributed to affected personnel in an attempt to learn the nature of the phenomenon. The journals contain the questions, reactions, and outcomes of the personnel.

Examples:

Dr. █████

Q: Why did ███████ cheat on me?
R: Disappointed
O: Has found answer after interrogating Dr. ███████

Janitor ██████████

Q: How did O5-12 even get to █████████?
R: Confused
O: Janitor ██████████ was detained and taken into custody, interviewed. O5-12 then administered Class A amnestics

Dr. ███

Q: Why did Wondertainment make the █████████████ product line?
R: Extreme confusion
O: Subject was unable to recieve an answer, thus requesting amnestics.

Dr. ███████████

Q: How did SCP-█████ go to that other narrative?
R: Confused, striken with anxiety
O: Detained, interrogated by O5-██, was administered Class B amnestics. O5-██ claims it as a good way to determine possible future SCP's

Hook/Attention Grabber: A very dangerous or beneficial infohazard, causes great curiosity among the infected. Causes you to question anything, everything.

Additional notes: I'd prefer this article to be a great motivation when it comes to philosophical ideals, and the act of always questioning. But why?

item.title: Question re: Editing others' articles
item.description: May we fix on-site links formatted as external links?
item.content:encoded:
Hi, I hope I've found the right place for site rules questions. My question's about this rule (emphasis mine):

Editing others' articles: You may correct grammar, spelling, or formatting errors on other peoples' articles. Please put a summary of changes in the 'description of changes' box. Any further edits require permission from the original author or Rewrite team.

Often, an on-site link (triple brackets) is formatted as an external link (single brackets). As the Google Chrome users among you may already know, these external links don't work for some users while they are logged in (because we visit scp-wiki.wikidot.com instead of scpwiki.com as a login workaround; visiting any link formatted as https://scpwiki.com/whatever gives us an error message1). Clicking a link that ought to be an on-site link and receiving an error is unpleasant, as is manually replacing scpwiki with scp-wiki.wikidot in the address bar.

I don't know if using the 'wrong' link type is technically a formatting error, but I am hoping to receive mod/admin confirmation that it falls under this category.2 Changing these links' format type would not alter the article text, it would just make the links work properly for those of us who have to use scp-wiki.wikidot.com instead of scpwiki.com for technical reasons.

Getting author permission each and every time, just to change link formatting type from external to on-site, would be hugely annoying for both the editor and the author. I am hoping that we readers can be allowed to make these formatting changes without obtaining author permission each time.

So, tl;dr: If a link is formatted as an external link, but would work properly as an on-site link, may we go ahead and make that formatting change without bothering the author for their permission?

Footnotes
1. Note that the error only appears when an external link specifies https. It's some sort of certificate recognition error. Links formatted as on-site links work fine for us Chrome users, because wikidot helpfully inserts whichever base address the reader is already using.
2. I actually created an account because I wanted to fix various minor errors as I came across them while reading.

item.title: The Though Farmer
item.description: An SCP that uses the 'thought energy' of people to gain more, and further its own objectives.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight
SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid SCP whose main objective appears to be the collection of, what will be labeled for ease of understanding, thought energy. The exact nature of this energy is unknown, however it is known that SCP-XXXX is able to use this energy to influence or cause events. SCP-XXXX typically gains this energy by gathering followers for cults or religions it leads or influences, however other methods have been recorded.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX begins its indoctrination process by introducing a cult it is involved with to it's target. SCP-XXXX then regularly manipulates it's target's focus to its cult via things the target enjoys. It is at this stage that the target decides to walk away, or become involved and proceed to the next stage. Eventually the target proceeds to the last stage. In this stage, the target becomes more engaged in cult activities which consumes a significant amount of the target's time. The target also sacrifices all 'optional' activities to make time for cult activities but still takes part in necessary daily activities, such as work, hygiene and eating. During this stage the target also has decreased cognitive functions. There is currently no known way to exit this stage, barring termination of the subject.

SCP-XXXX itself is a non-corporeal entity that is capable of appearing as almost any animal or person. SCP-XXXX is capable of appearing in the 'real' world as well as in the dreams of individuals. There has been no recorded physical interaction with SCP-XXXX, and it's incapable of moving objects. SCP-XXXX has also rarely interacted with foundation personnel.
SCP-XXXX current motives are unknown, however there are some conversations between foundation staff and SCP-XXXX that are in it's file.

Central Narrative: This SCP article focuses on SCP-XXXX's activities, what religions and cults SCP-XXXX has interfered with in history (that the foundation can find) SCP-XXXX's current endeavours, it's motives and communication with the foundation and, ultimately what it will do with its power (besides get more).

Hook: The hook (ATM) is the process that SCP-XXXX 'gains' additional people, as well as its interactions with the foundation and its end goal with what it wants to accomplish (Which will be a mystery, to maintain intrigue.).

Notes: While the whole emphasis on SCP-XXXX's motives and goals seems lacking in this post, I'll include some interactions with foundation personnel that will go more in depth.

item.title: Tale: Rabbit Seed-bombs
item.description: house is over run by an anomalous, self-perpetuating, rabbit warren
item.content:encoded:
A deprecated house is over run by an anomalous, self-perpetuating, rabbit warren and their poo. Their previous owners still occupy the house.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Dark Comedy

Elevator Pitch: Two Foundation agents are sent to investigate a house overrun by rabbits in the Midwest. The house is found to have its own microclimate similar to the Pacific Northwest, and its ecosystem is self-perpetuating due to the anomalous rabbits. The previous owners are turned into rabbit people by parasitic baby rabbits.

Central Narrative: It’s revealed through the found documents, an owner’s journals, that they had two rabbits. Before they could get them spade and neutered, the vets office closed due to quarantine. Unable to be contained, going so far as to teleport, the male rabbits kept escaping and creating more litters. The owners hired the city compost to take their quickly escalating piles of rabbit poo.

+ show block
– hide block

Over time, firs, ferns, blackberries, and other Pacific Northwest foliage grows out of the rabbit poo at an expedited rate. The owners, and housemates, slowly turn into rabbit-people when parasitic baby rabbits burrow into the base of their skulls. (Similar to the Goa’uld from Stargate).

Two Foundation agents are sent to investigate the house and they traverse room to room to figure out the ill fate of the owners. They are chased out of the house by angry rabbits, and rabbit-people.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A deprecated house is over run by an anomalous, self-perpetuating, rabbit warren and their poo. Their previous owners still occupy the house.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: Kamen Rider but it's SCP
item.description: I once threatened someone I'd write this, but is it any good?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: If you're going to get a Magic Man to help make your superhero dreams come true, be sure you know what the hell you're doing. Otherwise you'll turn your friends into bugs and make demons out of your little sister's cancer.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

A dumb teenager who's equal parts edgy and idealistic decides the world would be better if his favorite Japanese superhero were in it for realz. So he goes to his local Magic Man to ask for some magic, which he gets. He of course has no idea how to use it properly, so testing quickly starts going wrong. Using the magic superhero belt too long/too many times turns the wearer into a pile of bugs. Distraught after losing at least one friend, he reevaluates why he's doing this. The point of being a hero isn't doing cool moves or beating up bad guys, you see. It's about making a real change in the world. Cue a little bit more magic to try and help his little sister's cancer. Cancer turns into monsters/demons that can be fought in the real world, since you can't Rider Kick cancer without killing a little kid. Our protagonist vanishes after this, as does his sister.

This is later discovered by the Foundation after our would-be hero goes missing and cancer demons start terrorizing SoCal. The demons are the primary object, the belt is the secondary. Said demons can only be contained by someone using the belt (yes, this is a Thing What Makes You Fight Good skip, strike 1, I know), so you've got an MTF that's switching off different members being the 'hero' and fighting cancer demons while hoping desperately the next time they put it on, they don't turn into a pile of bugs. And that's about where the idea ends.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Man, if you're not already here to read SCP articles, I don't know how to hook you.

Additional Notes: Article will include hand-written journal entries with sketches, doodles and likely personally revealing notes.

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation works hard to cover up anomalies, having extensive measures to prevent word of the Paranormal getting out. But the internet is a popular thing, especially among conspiracy theorists.

Central Narrative: A simple anomaly is discovered by WWS. It's a frog that when a picture is taken of it, always produces the same photo. Further more, whenever an addition copy of the photo is created, physical or digital, a non-anomalous frog of the same type is formed in the vicinity. The main story of the article comes when a member of the Parawatch community gets their hands on one of the photos and discovers it's properties. They send it to the rest of Parawatch who continue to send it and copy it like crazy. The Foundation learns about it but their normal strategies such as taking the picture down and visual amnestics don't work due to the paranoia of Parawatch and them saving copies to hard-drives. This comes to a head when the Foundation resorts to a complete take-down of the Parawatch wiki and the physical administration of amnestics to all exposed members, draining significant resources and giving the Parawatch community a lot to speculate on. The article closes out with a note regarding the difficulty of maintaining the veil in the internet age and about being thankful the image wasn't memetic.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A simple anomaly and a non-anomalous group almost breaking the veil.

 Subject: Items: [Location]:Item ... Afterwards:

Elevator Pitch: A road on which objects relating to your past dreams, goals, and desires appear (out of reach). As you walk along it, past burdens are "freed" from you.

Central Narrative: Disconnected stories of the people that walk on the road, told by the objects that they encounter. For instance:

  • An burnt out ethics committee member who wanted to "bring justice" when he was younger (a discolored robe, a trap with a hole in it, a corroded pen,…, a colorless foundation site), after stepping off of the road he resigns from the foundation.
  • A terrorist who was a revolutionary. (A torn police cap, burnt money, a rusted guillotine,…, his own corpse), who puts up less resistance after.
  • A doctor who wanted to save lives. (A firefighter coat, a broken down gravestone,…, a hospital in the distance). Returned to foundation work with increased score on the Foundation Personnel Wellness Exam.
  • …
+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP aims to tell the story of people's lives through the test logs, which are just lists of items, without the "human" in them. There are no notes on theorized meanings, and the reader is free to draw their own conclusion from the objects and their location on the road.

Additional Notes: I don't quite know how "strong(?)" to make the effect of giving up your past dreams yet. Hey howdy hey, so I'm writing a tale at the moment that predominantly revolves around a crime scene. Thing is, I don't actually know very much about how actual crime scene procedures work, as the most popular point of reference tends to be dramatized TV shows.

I realise that in order to keep stuff interesting I'll need to strike a decent balance between real-world procedure and something a little more fictitious, but I'm not entirely sure where to look for real-world references. I've done some research, but I end up with a mixed bag of results that refer to how various countries handle it.

I'm looking for details of crime scene procedure as it would be in the real world particularly for the US - what kinda staff will be present, who's allowed where, how much can be done on-site that would contribute to the investigation, etc.
The crime takes place indoors (an apartment), and involves a dead body, if those details matter at all.

Articles for reference would be good, and if there's any online short story type deals that exist out there (I've had no luck finding any that aren't books) that would be fantastic.

Scp XXXX is a Reality Bender
Scp XXXX had been discovered in a cave near Quebec, Canada
Scp XXXX is spanned through time and space.

Central Narrative:
Scp XXXX was discovered by an Amateur Cave Explorer in 1973, in a cave near Quebec, Canada. The Amateur Cave Explorer was taken into Foundation custody and amnestisized, alongside all other civilians involved, after reporting to a local hospital, stating he heard a voice in his head talk about freeing himself from the wizards bonds. The Foundation learns Scp XXXX voice spreads into Humans Consciousness when any contact is made beit physical or verbal. The cave of origin is blocked and all Personnel that had been infected had been anesthetized. Scp XXXX is reclassified from euclid to safe. 14 years later, Dr. Mason Cooper reports hearing voices inside his head, though he had only been working for the Foundation for 11 years.

+ show block
– hide block

Staff had concluded that Personnel already infected by Scp XXXX previously had seemed to get reinfected. Though some personnel had either left the Foundation and been Anesthetized or were somewhere else in the world. Scp XXXX is reclassified as keter as it now spreads into the entire world. As more and more instances of Scp XXXX begin to be heard in peoples head the more mist and fog begins to surround Scp XXXX’s point of origin. Until at a Estimated 1 000 000 cases where the fog slowly turned into a human like form and moved into Montreal, Canada. The Foundation theorizes that Scp XXXX was sent across space and time by the Wizards in 1200, so any Instance of Scp XXXX would imbalance its containment as it would be more in one time then the others, meaning it would start to remeterialize. The Foundation enlists Mobile Task Force Simga 32 ( Tbh I Dont Any Good Mtf Who Travel Through Time ) To travel to Canada and release a amnestic and start a PowerGrid Failure to all of Quebec to stop the spread of Media related to Scp XXXX, Finally Sigma 32 puts down a temporal rift near the anomaly, sending all living creatures in the radius to various points in the future in order to contain it. Scp XXXX is currently pending classification of either safe or neutralized.

item.title: Buzzcut
item.description: A buzzer from the 1950's that grants you irresistible charisma.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Fantasy

Elevator Pitch: It's a barber buzzer. Upon using it on one's head, the individual starts receiving more attention than usual. Overtime, as hair grows, the attention diminishes, unless one cuts again, and instead attention increases. Attention, as well as sex appeal. Continuing the process allows the user to have increasing and overwhelming charisma to the extent that they can influence first people, then towns, then world events.

Central Narrative: The buzzer was found to be in the possession of an artifact dealer, and was purchased by the owner of a 50's themed diner to be placed in a safe with other memorabilia. Upon discovery by the Foundation, the dive owner says the girl he bought it from claims it was used by Elvis to cut his hair. After testing the piece is found to be non anamolous, placed in confinement, however an agent over the testing steals it to resell it, but not before trying it on his own head. He begins to notice his life change.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact the the influence builds on itself to make the user more and more powerful, and can be transferred if one single hair is buzzed on another man or woman. The buzzer also increases the physical strength of the individual and performance of physiological functions, to the extent that the user can not only become stronger than possible for a human, but also have a faster metabolism (speed), more god like features, and be a far greater sexy badboy/girl than humanly possible.

Additional Notes: After non-use of about a week, all influence dies out. It isn't saved within the buzzer. This is why, if the Elvis fact is true, Elvis, nor any of the other users' influence, is transferred to new users. Any stretch beyond humanly possible abilities granted by the buzzer is unnoticed by individuals, due to the overwhelming charisma, and is brushed off. There is no proper way to cut your hair with the buzzer, but upon doing so, everyone will love your haircut.

item.title: SCP-XXXX A blessed exchange
item.description: An object that exchanges two aspects(body parts/memories/facts) of a person for a new aspect.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Mystery

Page Layout: Object description and containment are minimal, and main focus will be on testing logs. There will be 10-15 of them, starting with mundane, and increasing in strangeness.

Elevator Pitch: The object swaps two aspects (body parts/memories/reality of their life) of a person with a new one, seemingly from its "collection" of obtained aspects. Since an unknown number of exchanges have occurred, over an unknown time/places, it has an unknowable number of aspects in its collection.

Central Narrative: Minimal. The testing logs will add mystery around the objects age/origins and purpose, suggesting alien/extra-dimensional life. Since the object can alter reality, detailed records and logs need to be kept in order to keep track of reality alterations.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The object removes aspects of a person and gives a brand new one. The removal of aspects could kill or dramatically change a person, even removing people/companies/ideas related to them. The new aspects can be memories, new organs, or reality altering itself as well. The testing logs will start with mundane things, eg gaining memories of another person, growing a new limb etc, and will progress to stranger exchanges where friends/family cease to exist, or they gain non-human knowledge. Adding to the intrigue is that every aspect "given" is assumed to have been taken at some stage, suggesting that the object has altered reality many times in the past in unknown ways.

item.title: The Zenwalker (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: A tragic complex story of a powerful entity playing hero
item.content:encoded:
A tragic complex story of a powerful entity playing hero only to become the only threat he ever had to worry about.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Cosmic Horror, Drama/Emotional,

Page Layout (Optional): This is going to be a rare case of and scp article in an scp article. There will be the normal containment procedures followed by a description then an addendum containing an scp article about this scp that he brought with him from the future (I know, bare with me). After the addendum, logs reviewing the interviews with the scp.

Elevator Pitch: Basically, this scp is an anomalous man from a different dimension in which the laws of physics are fundamentally different. It's because of this difference that he has the ability to manipulate gravity. His upbringing and childlike curiosity provided the perfect origin story for a modern superhero with a scientific alter ego. By day he was a lab coat pushing the limits of his abilities to fully understand gravity and it's effects, by night a merciless vigilante obliterating local crime with an iron fist.

+ show block
– hide block

Now, I know what it looks like but stay with me, this isn't just another superhero. In fact, the true danger of this scp came from his day job as a scientist. His continuous experiments yielded amazing discoveries about what he could do, but it eventually led to the collapse of the universe as we know it. The collapse of the universe damned him to just exist in an existence in which he was the only thing that excited. Madness had claimed him after a millennia of solitude, but he didn't spend his time in the void laying down. He used this time to further study his ability. Eventually he was able to feel the connection between time and gravity. This led his ability to manipulate time. From there he formulated a plan to send himself back in time to kill his younger self before he collapses the universe. However, do to his mental instability he was slain his younger self. That younger version of himself grew to repeat history/the future and collapsed the universe, went mad, discovered time travel, and repeated the plan to kill his younger self. This time however, he remembered how he defeated his older self and didn't fall for the same tactic he used when he was younger. This caused the fight to last a while longer than the first fight. However, the younger version of himself still came out on top do to his mental edge. This younger version of himself repeated the same cycle extending the fight just a bit longer. As the cycle continued the scale of the battle grew larger, so did the foundation's involvement. This only served to escalate the situation as it eventually led to a broken masquerade. This cycle repeated until the battle was the cause of the collapsed universe. The cycle finally ended when he decided to instead travel farther back in time and seek out the foundation to contain his younger self before he grows up to become a threat. The conversation with a mad man didn't get nearly as far as the scp article he brought back with him as proof of his claims. The article inside the article is the one he brought back with him and the over all article will be the whole story.

Central Narrative: It's a tragic story of a hero being his only threat. Eventually ending the narrative before it starts.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The very deeply rooted story.

Additional Notes: This is my first attribution to the site in general and I'm sure I have a lot to learn. This is me diving head first into a community I've loved for years and should have contributed to ages ago. All criticism welcome and appreciated.

item.title: Human Fungi
item.description: A fungi in which infects humans.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX represents a single species of fungi, currently only known to exist within northern Queensland, Australia. SCP-XXXX is similar to the genus Ophiocordyceps, as SCP-XXXX has the ability to infect Insectoids, Birds, and Mamalians including Humans. Once an individual has been infected with SCP-XXXX (now designated SCP-XXXX-1) during early stages will begin to suppress the individual's consciousness and hijack the brain. SCP-XXXX has the ability to tap into the memories of SCP-XXXX-1, because of this SCP-XXXX-1 are able to basic human things such as communicating, movement, etc

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX during late stages will use the SCP-XXXX-1 instance to move to a suitable location to multiply. Once achieved SCP-XXXX-1 will attach itself to a surface, as well as immobilising itself by placing a cocoon like structure around its body. From here spores will begin to fly out of SCP-XXXX-1, which will multiply SCP-XXXX

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Numerous SCP-XXXX-1 instances have been leaked (and deleted of course) however one was able to communicate directly to an non-infected individual via text. This is where the story will take place.

item.title: Your friendly neighborhood demon
item.description: A completely incompetent demon is summoned by a researcher
item.content:encoded:
A completely incompetent demon is summoned by a researcher. The researcher gets terminated and the demon tries (miserably) to do its job.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mostly comedy, secondly psychological.

Page Layout:

+ show block
– hide block

Class and ConProcs before and after the “incident”. Description of the Book and, adding the “as of dd/mm/yyyy” the description of the Entity. At least three Interview logs with the entity (or just one log with multiple “extracts” to give the idea). An example of a contract the entity would propose (with a lot of Latin and high-sounding words of jurisprudence to give it an overly serious characterization to contrast the demon’s one) and, finally, a note from Hell itself.

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP will be composed of two parts:
• A book, which the Foundation seized, that describes various thaumaturgical/satanical rituals. One of these being the summoning of demons.
• A weak and lower demon, summoned by a Researcher trying to bargain for money, power, etc. The demon is rather “stupid”. It’s forcibly stuck in the room he was summoned in due to the blood glyph drawn on the floor and his only goal is to acquire as many souls as he can.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The demon acts all high and mighty, like a stereotypical devil from fantasy literature, talking big and trying to sway people into making contracts with it. It is, however, extremely weak and incompetent. Gets easily irritated, lies terribly, and doesn’t seem to be able to trick anyone into doing anything evil. Quite on the contrary it seems that people behave better around him, much to its irritation.
Meanwhile through the interview logs the reader experiences the reaction to the loss of the researcher that summoned it, that was terminated for his abuse. The conversations with the demon will parallel a possible set of reactions to the Foundation methods in dealing with rule breakers.
In the end a note will be found in the site director’s office thanking the Foundation for containing the demon without exorcising him back, humorously hinting that the demon was so incompetent that he was disliked in Hell.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

Most of the article features a comedic style derived from the stereotypical “big demon” behavior being attributed to such a wimpy and incapable creature, its inefficient methods and, lastly his frustration about it.
On the other side readers will delve into some possible reactions to the idea that someone you worked with every day, maybe even dated or considered a friend, has been literally killed for breaking the rules at work. Even if working at the Foundation they are still human beings after all.

Additional Notes:

+ show block
– hide block

Hiding behind a copious humorous screen there will be a cynical reasoning about the Foundation methods and, above all, their impact on personnel. I think this "laugh and think" style could prove functional.
